report.source_text: The patient was given acetazolamide, aspirin, ocular massage, and a combination of dorzolamide and timolol. She was monitored biweekly to assess visual acuity and intraocular pressure (IOP) for 12 weeks, followed by evaluations every 8 weeks for 6 months, then biannual check-ups for 2 years. At 6 weeks, after resolution of the preretinal hemorrhages, panretinal photocoagulation was performed to prevent neovascular glaucoma, which is associated with central retinal vein occlusion within 90 days. It was performed prophylactically as the patient resides in a remote area and was unwilling to adhere to a regular follow-up schedule. Intravitreal antivascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) was not used, as no macular edema was observed on OCT. By the 12th week, the patient’s vision was 6/36, with an IOP of 12 mmHg in the left eye.

clinician.final_diagnosis: central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO) accompanied by ciliary retinal artery (CLRA) occlusion secondary to oral contraceptive pills (OCPs)
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 28-year-old Pakistani female, 3.5 months postpartum after cesarean section and with recent 25-day use of progestin-only oral contraceptive pills, presented with sudden painless vision loss in the left eye for 3 hours. Initial examination revealed counting fingers vision, relative afferent pupillary defect, and normal intraocular pressure. Dilated fundus examination demonstrated classic CRVO findings (optic disc edema, 360-degree preretinal hemorrhages, venous tortuosity, cotton wool spots) plus a white ischemic area nasal to the fovea suggestive of ciliary retinal artery occlusion. OCT confirmed inner retinal hyperreflectivity consistent with arterial occlusion, and FFA demonstrated delayed dye filling of the ciliary retinal artery. Comprehensive hypercoagulability screening (including factor V Leiden, antiphospholipid antibodies, protein C/S) was negative, as were autoimmune profiles, carotid Doppler, and echocardiography. The patient was managed with acetazolamide, aspirin, ocular massage, topical dorzolamide/timolol, and prophylactic panretinal photocoagulation at 6 weeks. By 12 weeks, vision improved to 6/36. The diagnosis of CRVO with CLRA occlusion secondary to OCPs was established by the dual vascular occlusion pattern on multimodal imaging, exclusion of inherited and acquired thrombophilias, and temporal association with recent OCP exposure in the absence of traditional vascular risk factors.
